cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: What Was the Plan?
cards.instruction: Find out what was promised, scheduled, or changed without revealing that you lost track.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Tomorrow's hike: ridge or river? I'm checking the weather against our route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ridge. We changed because the river path flooded.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Flood warning, then. Where are we meeting? I'll add that to the reminder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've asked me that twice. Have you forgotten your own itinerary?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm checking it works without my help. Brief me like a new recruit; I'll take notes, starting with where I report.

mechanism: A approves a subordinate briefing as a quality check while using it to recover a forgotten route and meeting place.
confusable: Fake expertise concerns competence generally; D30 specifically hides losing track of agreed plans while extracting their content.
comparison: A hiking reminder and repeated-question challenge differ from private dinner invitation proofreading.
seedUse: Use D30-b route correction and accusation of forgetting, with S01 approving a briefing rather than adopting an unexplained lower-status role.
